source.title: A thalamo-amygdalar circuit underlying the extinction of remote fear memories

confidence_rationale: Multi-method causal circuit dissection (viral tracing, activity mapping, fiber photometry, chemogenetics, closed-loop optogenetics) shows nucleus reuniens (NRe) inputs to basolateral amygdala (BLA) register and transmit safety signals that drive remote fear extinction: NRe-to-BLA activity rises just before freezing cessation, inhibition impairs and activation facilitates extinction. Strong support for an ACTIVE, transmitted safety-prediction signal (MECH-304's conditioned-inhibition / safety-transmission role) as a distinct circuit from threat and from relief-reward substrate. Source quality very high (causal, bidirectional, cross-validated with human imaging cited in paper). Mapping fidelity moderate: MECH-304 names a cortico-striatal encoding + IL-to-CeA expression substrate, whereas Silva adds a midline-THALAMIC (reuniens) node to BLA -- supports the active-safety-transmission premise but extends the named anatomy. Transfer risk low-moderate.
failure_signatures: Safety transmission here is THALAMO-amygdalar (reuniens->BLA), a node not currently in MECH-303/304's stated substrate (prefrontal-hippocampal / cortico-striatal + IL-CeA) -- the REE safety substrate as written may be anatomically incomplete (missing a thalamic relay).
The NRe-to-BLA safety signal is specific to REMOTE (30-day) but not recent (1-day) fear extinction -- a time-since-encoding dependence that no current REE safety mechanism represents.

If REE treated safety as identical to relief, this would weaken it: the safety-transmission circuit (reuniens->BLA, suppressing fear) is anatomically separate from the relief-completion reward circuit (NAc/VTA).

mapping.source_claim_statement: Extinction of remote (30-day-old) fear memories depends on nucleus reuniens (midline thalamus) inputs to the basolateral amygdala; NRe-to-BLA inputs activate during remote extinction, are potentiated upon fear reduction, and both total NRe and monosynaptic NRe-to-BLA activity increase shortly before freezing cessation -- i.e. the NRe registers and transmits safety signals to the BLA. Inhibition impairs, activation facilitates, remote fear extinction.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-304: a discrete predictive structure encoding 'this stimulus actively predicts that suffering will be omitted', whose output pathway gates the release of avoidance/fear and which is updated by relief-completion (MECH-302) events. Silva grounds the ACTIVE safety-transmission half of the safety system -- a transmitted inhibitory signal that suppresses an established threat representation -- distinct from MECH-303's passive contextual store and from MECH-302's reward-circuit offset reinforcement.
mapping.mapping_caveat: MECH-304's stated substrate is cortico-striatal encoding + IL-to-CeA expression; Silva's circuit is reuniens(thalamus)-to-BLA and is specific to remote (consolidated) fear. The paper supports the existence and causal role of an active transmitted safety signal that gates fear release, but it implicates a thalamic relay and a time-since-encoding dependence not captured in MECH-304 as written. Read as support for the active-safety-prediction premise plus a flag to broaden the named anatomy, not a confirmation of MECH-304's specific cortico-striatal wiring.
mapping.source_context: Mouse, viral tracing + activity mapping + fiber photometry + chemogenetic + closed-loop optogenetic manipulation; remote vs recent contextual/cued fear extinction; human imaging corroboration cited in paper.

confidence_components.notes: Exceptional causal circuit evidence for active safety transmission; the fidelity discount is the anatomical mismatch (thalamic relay vs MECH-304's cortico-striatal/IL-CeA wording). Net 0.80 -- the active-safety-prediction premise is strongly supported even where the exact substrate differs.
